Please rewrite this messy layout into clean, readable HTML + CSS with good spacing and structure.

Here's a chunk of code:
  [paste code]. Help me break it down into logical blocks and explain the purpose of each part in plain language.

Can you simulate how this code would run and point out anything that might crash, fail, or return something weird?

Can you help me find missing or incorrect imports, mismatched brackets, or small typos that might be causing bugs in this code?

Can you make the whole app use a consistent color palette and fix anything that looks out of place?

Help me make this app dark mode-friendly. Add the necessary styles and make sure everything still looks good.

Give me Tailwind (or CSS) code for a UI card that includes:
  (image + title + button) with hover and dark mode support.

Make this layout look good on both desktop and mobile without me needing to learn CSS.

Suggest a better file structure or modular breakdown for this code:
  [paste code or describe file], using common best practices in this stack.

This layout feels cramped. Can you add more breathing room and improve the spacing?

Build a clean, modern form with inputs for (list of fields), and include basic client-side validation using (framework or vanilla JS).

Can you make this whole page look like a modern SaaS app, without changing the logic?

I want to create a responsive layout using CSS grid or flexbox that supports (number) columns on desktop and stacks on mobile. Help me scaffold it.

Create a responsive navigation bar with a mobile drawer menu. Keep it minimal and avoid using external libraries.

Draft some scaffolding code that sets up this app with minimal boilerplate.

Transform this into a modern startup-like landing page with clean design patterns.

Add just enough animation or transitions to make this app feel smoother -- but nothing flashy or over-the-top.

Can you adjust the fonts and spacing in this app so it's easier to read and looks more balanced?

This UI feels kind of ugly or messy. Can you clean it up and make it look more modern and polished?

prompts.title: Writing Prompts
prompts.description: Evaluate the strategy's alignment with our long-term vision and mission. Identify any discrepancies and recommend modifications to ensure cohesive progress towa...
prompts.template:
Evaluate the strategy's alignment with our long-term vision and mission. Identify any discrepancies and recommend modifications to ensure cohesive progress towards our overarching goals. [PASTE HERE:
  Organizational vision statement and strategy document]

Rewrite this content to match the style of [author or tone, e.g. clear, direct, conversational], with an emphasis on readability and tone consistency.

Help me write a thought leadership post for product managers about how to scope AI-powered features responsibly. I want to share a contrarian take and back it up with examples from recent projects.

Write a blog post about how I'm thinking through whether to rebuild our internal CLI tool. I want it to sound exploratory, surface pros and cons, and invite input from others in similar roles.

Propose a set of coherent actions that operationalize the guiding policies. For each action, detail the implementation steps, responsible parties, and expected outcomes. [PASTE HERE:
  Guiding policies and available resources]

Help me come up with creative and relevant names for [app/team/bot/project/blog/repo], ideally with a theme or tone like [funny/professional/clever/etc.].

Write a closing paragraph for a blog post about debugging distributed systems. I want to leave readers with a clear takeaway, a reminder to be patient with themselves, and an invitation to share their own stories.

I want to write a white paper explaining why our company should invest in building a centralized developer platform. Help me structure it with a strong executive summary, a case for change, proposed solution, business impact, and implementation risks.

Write a proposal for adding error tracking to our frontend app using Sentry. I want to explain the current gap, how Sentry would help, what it would cost us (in time or complexity), and the tradeoffs.

I want to write a blog post for early-career engineers about how feature flags can reduce risk in deployments. Can you generate a title, a strong intro hook, and a clear outline with 3-5 key points?

Help me draft a technical white paper introducing our new architecture for scaling GitHub Actions workflows. Include background context, limitations of our old system, technical design, and a performance comparison.

Develop guiding policies to address the identified challenges. Each policy should outline the intended direction, the trade-offs involved, and how it aligns with our organizational goals. [PASTE HERE:
  List of challenges and organizational objectives]

Convert this content into a clear and well-structured markdown file or blog post, formatted for easy sharing or publication.

Write the opening paragraph of a blog post called 'Why You Should Treat Onboarding Like a Production System.' It should be thought-provoking, punchy, and hook readers in the first sentence.

Write a personal reflection on what I learned from launching a product that failed. I want it to be honest, useful to other builders, and focused on lessons I didn't expect to learn.

Write a funny, clever, or memorable slogan or title for [event/initiative/project], optionally drawing on pop culture or common inside jokes.

Translate the strategy into a communication plan tailored for different stakeholders (e.g., engineers, product managers, executives). For each audience, outline the key messages, preferred communication channels, and engagement strategies. [PASTE HERE:
  Finalized strategy document]

Rewrite this content to match the style of [author or tone, e.g. clear, direct, conversational], with an emphasis on readability and tone consistency.

prompts.title: Social Media
prompts.description: Help me draft a post that shares a behind-the-scenes look at a product feature we launched. Keep it concise, include one interesting decision we made, and end w...
prompts.template:
Help me draft a post that shares a behind-the-scenes look at a product feature we launched. Keep it concise, include one interesting decision we made, and end with a prompt that invites feedback or stories. [Paste the feature name, why it matters, and any internal insight.]

Help me write a "build in public" update about [PROJECT/FEATURE]. Share the progress I've made, challenges I faced, and what I learned along the way.

Write a quick LinkedIn post that shares a moment of career advice I wish I'd known earlier. Make it sound like something I'd tell a junior teammate over coffee. [PASTE HERE:
  your piece of advice and a short example of when it would have helped you.]

Help me write insightful commentary to accompany this chart/data visualization about [TOPIC]. Include the key takeaway and why it matters.

I want to share a short, visual tip related to [PASTE HERE:
  your role or niche, e.g., productivity, design, engineering, solo building]. Help me write a caption that gives one piece of practical advice in 2-3 lines, paired with a clean photo or graphic.

Help me write a caption for a 'day in the life' photo or reel. It should be light, relatable, and include 1 quirky or unexpected detail. [PASTE HERE:
  what the post is about and one behind-the-scenes moment or habit.]

I want to post a 'what I wish I knew earlier' tip for people earlier in their journey. Help me write a short caption that's encouraging, experience-backed, and skimmable. [PASTE HERE:
  the lesson, when you learned it, and how it changed your approach.]

Help me write a post that shares a career milestone (promotion, job change, anniversary), but keeps the tone grounded and reflective -- not overly self-congratulatory. [Paste the milestone and a few sentences on how you're feeling or what you've learned.]

Help me turn this idea into a compelling post. Structure it as a short story with a clear takeaway.

I want to share a bit about what I'm learning as a PM working on AI/infra/productivity tools. Draft a post that includes 1-2 insights, one thing I didn't expect, and a question for others in the space. [Include the topic and any context you've been thinking about.]

Turn this internal reflection into a public-facing post that's useful to others. Keep the message clear, actionable, and human. [Paste a few bullet points or a voice note summary of what you've been thinking about.]

Write a tweet that shares a lesson learned from a recent build, launch, or failure. Keep it concise, useful, and ideally quotable. [PASTE HERE:
  short version of what happened and what you learned.]

Help me write a carousel-style caption with 3-5 lessons I learned from this experience. Each slide should be a punchy takeaway, with the final slide as a reflection. [PASTE HERE:
  quick story or summary of the experience -- a launch, challenge, or aha moment.]

Help me create a short 3-5 post "microthread" about this insight:
  [INSIGHT]. Each post should be concise but valuable, building on the previous one.

Draft a personal reflection post about how my thinking has evolved on this topic. Make it thoughtful, not preachy -- I want to show growth over time. [PASTE HERE:
  topic or belief, what you used to think, what changed, and why.]

Write a post that shares a small but useful tip related to my work in [PASTE HERE:
  industry or role, like PM, engineering, AI product strategy]. I want it to be practical, something others can try today.

Help me break down this process into clear, sequential steps:
  [DESCRIBE PROCESS]. Make it easy to follow and actionable.

Help me write a LinkedIn post that unpacks a product or design decision we made. It should show the thinking behind the scenes -- not just the end result. [PASTE HERE:
  what the decision was, what tradeoffs were involved, and why you chose what you did.]

I need to announce the launch of [PRODUCT/FEATURE NAME].

Key details:
- What it does:
  [DESCRIPTION]
- Main benefits:
  [BENEFITS]
- Target audience:
  [AUDIENCE]
- Launch date:
  [DATE]

Create a compelling social media announcement that generates excitement and clearly communicates the value.

Write a professional LinkedIn post about a recent project I wrapped up. It should highlight what the project accomplished, a key challenge we overcame, and a reflection on what I learned as a PM/engineer/leader. [Paste a short summary of the project, your role, and any lessons or surprising moments.]

Write a compelling Instagram caption that tells a quick story about a recent project or moment of progress. Make it real, short, and end with a call to action like 'What's something you've built this week?' [PASTE HERE:
  1-2 sentence story about what you made, fixed, learned, or shipped.]

Turn this outline into a compelling post that summarizes a talk I gave (or am preparing to give). Highlight 1-2 big takeaways, and invite others to share their perspective. [PASTE HERE:
  title or theme of the talk, key points, and your main message.]

Write a caption for a reel that shows a before → after transformation (in process, mindset, design, workflow, etc.). Keep it punchy and tie it back to the bigger lesson. [PASTE HERE:
  what changed, what the shift looked like, and what you realized.]

I want to share a short, visual tip related to [PASTE HERE:
  your role or niche, e.g., productivity, design, engineering, solo building]. Help me write a caption that gives one piece of practical advice in 2-3 lines, paired with a clean photo or graphic.

Turn this personal insight into an Instagram post that feels like a journal entry. I want to be real, a little vulnerable, but still useful to others in similar roles. [PASTE HERE:
  what you realized, how it hit you, and why it matters now.]

Write a LinkedIn post that turns this small work win into a teachable moment for others in tech. Keep it humble, but highlight the lesson learned. [PASTE HERE:
  1-2 sentences about what you shipped or fixed, and what surprised you.]

prompts.title: Program Management
prompts.description: Act as a TPM helping frame kickoff messaging for cross-functional alignment. The program has ambitious goals, but teams are unclear about their role and impact....
prompts.template:
Act as a TPM helping frame kickoff messaging for cross-functional alignment. The program has ambitious goals, but teams are unclear about their role and impact. Write a 1-slide summary that explains the "why now," shared goals, and how each org contributes. Be confident, collaborative, and motivating. Provide two headline options: one product-centric, one infrastructure-focused. Use this background to help craft the message: [PASTE HERE: list of goals, teams involved, and a short description of urgency or opportunity].

"Analyze our cross-team planning process. Identify the top 3 friction points slowing execution. For each, write a 2-sentence summary of the issue, its impact, and a recommended fix. Focus on visibility, dependencies, and prioritization. [PASTE:
  Planning doc or initiative board]"

"Create a milestone tracking template for this project. For each milestone: 1) Include a specific, measurable deliverable, 2) Define 2-3 clear success criteria, 3) Identify key dependencies, 4) Suggest 1-2 leading indicators we can track. Format as a concise, scannable doc that helps maintain momentum. [PASTE: Project overview]"

Act as a Technical Program Manager writing a program update for VP-level stakeholders. The project is on track, but a key dependency slipped and a decision is pending. Write a weekly status update using this format: Highlights, Risks, Decisions Needed, Next Steps. Keep it tight, transparent, and confidence-inspiring. Provide one version as a Slack message and another as a slide blurb. Source the details from this summary: [PASTE HERE: bullet list of key wins, current blockers, and upcoming milestones].

Help me break down this project into a series of 1-2 week sprints. For each sprint, outline: 1) A clear theme/focus, 2) Key deliverables, 3) Major dependencies, and 4) Areas of uncertainty or risk. Focus on a high-level timeline view that helps me understand the overall flow without getting stuck in details. [PASTE: Project description and overall timeline]

Act as a TPM assisting with execution planning for a complex infra refactor. The project requires staged rollout, testing, migration support, and backend contract changes. Create a phase-based execution plan with timelines, dependencies, and major engineering milestones. Prioritize clarity and alignment. Give one version optimized for Google Sheets and another for a Notion roadmap doc. Base your plan on the following: [PASTE HERE: current state of infra, project goals, known phases or staging needs].

"Help me draft a problem statement for this initiative. Include: 1) Clear articulation of the underlying issue, 2) Measurable impact on users/business, 3) High-level goal we want to achieve. Make it actionable without prescribing specific solutions. Keep it under 200 words. [PASTE: Background context of the initiative]"

"Review the following program portfolio and categorize each program into one of three buckets:
  (1) aligned and high-performing, (2) at risk or behind, and (3) misaligned or redundant. Return the output as a table with program name, current owner, priority level, and a 1-sentence rationale. [PASTE PROGRAM LIST]"

Act as a cross-functional program analyst and risk strategist. This initiative spans infrastructure, security, and product. Identify 5 program-level risks and assign each a potential mitigation tactic. Organize them in a table: Risk, Impact, Owner, Mitigation. Write with precision for a senior engineering audience. Provide two sets: one focused on delivery risks, another on strategic alignment risks. Use the following context to guide your analysis: [PASTE HERE: short description of the initiative, participating teams, and goals].

"Create a comprehensive program status report template for our [PROJECT NAME] program. The report should include the following sections:

1. Executive Summary
2. Key Milestones & Achievements
3. Current Status by Workstream
4. Risks & Issues
5. Dependencies
6. Budget Status
7. Resource Allocation
8. Decisions Needed
9. Next Steps

For each section, provide a clear structure with bullet points or tables as appropriate, and include 2-3 example entries to demonstrate the format. The report should be concise yet thorough, suitable for executive stakeholders with limited time."

"Help me create a stakeholder communication plan for [PROJECT/PROGRAM NAME]. The plan should include the following components:

1. Stakeholder Analysis
   - Identify key stakeholder groups
   - Assess their interest and influence levels
   - Determine information needs for each group

2. Communication Goals & Strategy
   - Primary objectives of communication
   - Key messages for different audiences
   - Timing and cadence considerations

3. Communication Matrix
   - Who:
  Stakeholder groups
   - What:
  Message content
   - When:
  Frequency
   - How:
  Communication channels
   - Who's responsible:
  Team member

4. Feedback Mechanisms
   - How stakeholder feedback will be collected
   - Process for incorporating feedback

Please provide a template with examples that I can easily adapt for my specific project/program needs."

Help me draft a [weekly/monthly] update for stakeholders on [project name]. Include:
  1) Key accomplishments since last update, 2) Current progress against goals, 3) Blockers or challenges we're facing, and 4) Upcoming priorities. Keep it concise, professional, and focused on information that matters to stakeholders.

Act as a TPM contributing to annual planning across product, platform, and security teams. The org is debating priorities between reliability, developer experience, and scale. Draft a strategic planning memo outlining 3 high-leverage bets we could invest in next year. Be data-informed and scenario-based. Provide three framing options: user-impact-first, cost-efficiency-first, and technical foundation-first. Base this on current plans: [PASTE HERE: strategy themes, relevant OKRs, and high-priority initiatives].

Act as an expert TPM with experience launching high-scale backend systems. I'm kicking off a multi-quarter program to unify telemetry across products. Write a first draft of a program charter that includes: purpose, scope, success metrics, stakeholders, and known risks. Make it concise and executive-ready. Generate two versions -- one formal for leadership, one more detailed for engineering teams. Use this input: [PASTE HERE: description of the program's intent, timeline, and any existing notes or expectations].

Act as a TPM writing a retrospective for a recently completed technical initiative. The project was delivered on time but revealed gaps in triage tooling and stakeholder alignment. Draft a retrospective report with sections: Goals, Wins, Challenges, Lessons Learned, Next Steps. Use a professional and constructive tone. Generate two versions: one full-length for docs, one short for email. Use this initiative summary: [PASTE HERE: high-level project summary, key outcomes, and any documented challenges].

prompts.title: Documentation
prompts.description: Turn this long article into a 3-sentence summary with the main argument and implications.
prompts.template:
Turn this long article into a 3-sentence summary with the main argument and implications.

Give me a high-level summary of this API doc, and include an example of how to use it.

Summarize this blog post and suggest what action a developer might take after reading it.

Create a presentation version of this blog post or internal memo. Break it into slide-friendly chunks with titles, key bullets, and optional visuals. [PASTE HERE:
  full blog post or doc you want to convert.]

Create a TL;DR version of this changelog, focused on what a developer needs to know.

Edit this text to improve clarity, reduce ambiguity, and make it more concise -- especially for an audience with limited time.

I need to explain this complex technical topic to a non-technical audience. Help me turn it into 4-5 slides with analogies, simplified visuals, and real-world examples. [PASTE HERE:
  the topic, and what audience you're presenting to.]

Convert this document into a decision-making doc (similar to Amazon's 1-pagers or PR/FAQs). Reformat it so the purpose, context, risks, alternatives, and recommendation are clear. [PASTE HERE:
  informal or scattered planning content.]

Extract all action items, decisions made, and follow-ups from these documents. Format them into a checklist with owner names (if available). [PASTE HERE:
  meeting notes, standup logs, or planning docs.]

Turn these docs into a single, easy-to-skim synthesis. Group information by theme or topic and remove redundant or outdated content. [PASTE HERE:
  any combination of docs you want merged -- e.g., brainstorm notes, specs, or research summaries.]

Compare the viewpoints or priorities across these documents and identify where they align, where they differ, and where there are conflicts or gaps. [PASTE HERE:
  multiple stakeholder docs, project briefs, or competing proposals.]

Rewrite this document as if it were a brief for an exec -- remove detail, emphasize outcomes, clarify ownership, and cut the fluff. [PASTE HERE:
  original draft, team writeup, or planning doc.]

Analyze the following documents and create a 1-page executive summary that includes key themes, major decisions, and open questions. Make it suitable for someone who hasn't read the full documents. [PASTE HERE:
  all relevant meeting notes, strategy docs, or planning memos.]

Turn these fragmented notes into a coherent draft memo or strategy doc. Keep the voice professional, focused, and outcome-oriented. [PASTE HERE:
  scattered notes, bullet points, or Slack excerpts.]

Summarize these docs into a 'How We Got Here' timeline that shows the evolution of our thinking, decisions, and direction. Useful for onboarding or retrospectives. [PASTE HERE:
  sequential docs, roadmap versions, meeting notes, or strategy shifts.]

Summarize this [article/blog/video/documentation] in 1-2 bullet points, focusing on the most valuable insight or practical takeaway.

Help me rewrite this investor deck for clarity and impact. Emphasize the problem, traction, and unique advantage -- without buzzwords. [PASTE HERE:
  current deck content or summary of each slide.]

Extract all key metrics or data points from this doc and explain what each one means in simple language. If there are trends or patterns, summarize them in 2-3 sentences. [PASTE HERE:
  performance report, OKR update, analytics review, etc.]

Extract all the key terms or acronyms from this doc and define them in context.

Turn these raw meeting notes into a 3-slide presentation that summarizes the discussion, decisions made, and proposed next steps. [PASTE HERE:
  messy meeting notes or transcript.]

From this meeting transcript or notes, extract a structured list of proposals, challenges raised, concerns flagged, and agreed-upon next steps. [PASTE HERE:
  raw meeting notes, Zoom transcript, or shared doc.]

Turn this documentation into onboarding notes for a new engineer joining the team.

Summarize this document in plain language, highlighting the key takeaways in bullet points.

Act as a presentation coach. Read this deck and give me 1) the main message per slide, 2) any slides that feel redundant or off-topic, and 3) suggestions to improve flow. [PASTE HERE:
  slide list, speaker notes, or deck outline.]

What problem is this document trying to solve, and what solution is it recommending?

Turn this internal doc into a short, public-friendly summary I could share as a blog, update, or internal post. Keep it human, jargon-free, and outcome-oriented. [PASTE HERE:
  long-form doc, design writeup, or research brief.]

Summarize these research documents into a brief that includes key findings, supporting evidence, and implications for product direction. Make it easy to share with PMs and leadership. [PASTE HERE:
  user research reports, survey results, or customer interviews.]

"Turn this research or data report into a presentation that shows: (1) the key insights, (2) trends over time, and (3) recommendations based on the findings. [PASTE HERE: data dump, research summary, or analytics doc.]"

Combine these product or feature writeups into a unified roadmap summary. Include the problem each feature solves, high-level implementation notes, and priority level if mentioned. [PASTE HERE:
  feature briefs, Jira tickets, or product docs.]

Turn these docs into a shared understanding artifact -- something a new team member could read to get up to speed. It should include the why, what, how, and key people involved. [PASTE HERE:
  multiple docs, briefs, or tickets across a project or stream of work.]

Create a side-by-side comparison of these two documents. Highlight similarities, differences, and where information is missing or contradictory. [PASTE HERE:
  two versions of a proposal, plan, or design doc.]

"Review this deck and tell me: which slides are too detailed, which need more context, and what could be moved to an appendix. [PASTE HERE: slide content or outline.]"

Help me design a slide for this message: [PASTE HERE: what you want to say]. Suggest a title, 3 concise bullets, and a simple visual or chart idea to support it.

Rewrite these slides to improve clarity, tone, and visual flow. Remove jargon, simplify headlines, and suggest better slide titles. [PASTE HERE:
  slide text or exported presentation content.]

Extract the key takeaways from this presentation and rewrite them as a slide-by-slide speaker script. Each note should include the core point, data callout (if any), and a sentence that ties it back to the audience's goals. [PASTE HERE:
  deck outline or slide text.]

Extract the so what from these documents -- what are the implications, hidden assumptions, or important decisions these docs suggest without saying directly? [PASTE HERE:
  product specs, strategy docs, or team notes.]

Help me rewrite this document so that it's optimized for stakeholder review. Clarify language, tighten structure, and make sure the 'ask' or decision is crystal clear. [PASTE HERE:
  your draft proposal, one-pager, or product pitch.]

What are the steps described here, and where are there potential gaps or assumptions?

"Make this slide deck more story-driven. Rewrite the headlines and flow to walk through: (1) the problem, (2) the tension, (3) the opportunity, and (4) our solution. [PASTE HERE: deck headlines or slide text.]"

"Act as a strategic reviewer. Read this doc and tell me: 1) what's missing, 2) what's unclear, and 3) what questions a skeptical reader would ask. [PASTE HERE: roadmap, product spec, or decision doc.]"

Write a 'for humans' explainer that turns this technical documentation into something a non-engineering stakeholder could understand. Focus on clarity and impact, not code. [PASTE HERE:
  technical specs, infra docs, or architectural plans.]

Give me specific examples or templates for [workflow/document/training], especially ones that are actionable and beginner-friendly.

Extract all timelines, dependencies, and blockers from these planning documents. Create a bulleted checklist organized by owner, priority, and sequence. [PASTE HERE:
  cross-functional plans, epic writeups, or initiative kickoffs.]

Help me extract the top 3 insights from each of these documents, then combine those into one overall takeaway per theme. [PASTE HERE:
  research, reports, interviews, or strategy writeups.]

Break this tutorial into a checklist of actions with expected outcomes for each step.

Identify the most frequently mentioned problems, goals, or user needs across these docs. Create a summary that shows patterns or themes. [PASTE HERE:
  user feedback, internal strategy docs, customer call transcripts, or surveys.]

Summarize these updates into a weekly team presentation with one slide per key theme. Keep it short and skimmable, but include callouts for action items or blockers. [PASTE HERE:
  doc, Slack summary, or Notion update.]

prompts.title: Deep Research
prompts.description: Find successful apps launched in the last 2 years in adjacent spaces (e.g., calendar tools, habit trackers, writing apps). For each:
prompts.template:
Find successful apps launched in the last 2 years in adjacent spaces (e.g., calendar tools, habit trackers, writing apps). For each:
  outline what made them successful (e.g., UX, niche focus, community), how they got early traction, and how they evolved their monetization model.

Summarize what early-stage app users in the target audience complain about most in similar tools. Pull insights from Reddit, Twitter, App Store reviews, and niche forums.

I'm trying to reduce time-to-first-value (TTFV) in our B2B SaaS onboarding. Research onboarding best practices and patterns used by modern SaaS products. Include UX examples (screenshots or flow descriptions), any known metrics or benchmarks, and tactics that reduce friction (e.g., templates, data import, AI assistants).

Help me draft a strategy doc on AI agent orchestration in software workflows. I want to understand how companies like Replit (with Ghostwriter), GitHub (with Copilot Agents), and emerging startups are thinking about agent architecture, coordination, and memory. Include tradeoffs they've discussed, challenges in implementation, and diagrams or architecture models if available.

Collect 3-5 real-world case studies where AI tools (e.g., Copilot, Cody, internal LLMs) were used to improve software development velocity. For each case:
  include who implemented it, what the AI was used for (e.g., test generation, code suggestions, PR review), measurable outcomes, and links to deeper writeups or talks.

What are the emerging trends in AI-assisted developer tooling from 2024 to early 2025? Identify tools that are gaining traction (like Cursor, Codeium, Cody), investor sentiment from recent VC funding rounds, and community perspectives from Hacker News, Reddit, and Twitter. Group findings by category (autocomplete, test generation, debugging, etc.).

Provide examples of how top-tier product teams have embedded AI into existing workflows without disrupting UX. Focus on features like summarization, smart suggestions, or prioritization. Include rollout strategies (e.g., beta toggles, usage caps), UI/UX integration patterns, and user adoption or retention metrics where available.

I'm drafting a strategy doc for launching a new AI-powered feature. Help me research how competitors messaged similar launches -- pull headlines, landing page copy, changelog entries, blog posts, and product walkthroughs from the last 18 months. Focus on framing, benefits language, and tone.

I need frameworks that PMs use to prioritize AI features. Focus on tradeoff-heavy decisions (e.g., explainability vs accuracy, automation vs human control). Include real-world examples from tools like Grammarly, GitHub Copilot, or Notion AI, and quote PMs or designers where possible.

I'm thinking about adding AI features like summarization, auto-tagging, or writing assistance. What are the most common implementation patterns in small apps? Include model choices (OpenAI vs open-source), latency tradeoffs, and UI/UX integrations that feel seamless.

I'm thinking of building an AI-powered productivity app for individuals. Help me identify the top 3 unsolved pain points people still experience with tools like Notion, Todoist, and ClickUp. Prioritize recent feedback (2023-2025) from power users and casual users alike.

Explore technical options for building an AI-native app with offline capabilities. Compare Electron vs Tauri vs Flutter vs React Native for cross-platform desktop or mobile use, and include examples of apps built on each stack with similar goals.

Explore the pros and cons of building versus buying analytics tooling (e.g., Segment, Mixpanel, internal dashboards) for a mid-stage SaaS company. Include technical debt, time-to-value, customization tradeoffs, and perspectives from engineering, data, and product teams. Include recent blog posts, conference talks, or postmortems.

Help me write a founder's one-pager for this app idea. I want to include the problem, audience, proposed solution, why now, and key differentiators. Use examples of real founder decks or YC applications to shape the language.

Give me a market analysis of tools solving the same core problem as my app idea. Include direct and indirect competitors, their positioning, pricing models, unique features, and gaps in the market based on recent user feedback.

Compare app pricing models based on app type (e.g., solo productivity, developer tooling, creative tools). Include what price points users are willing to pay in each category, and what factors help justify premium pricing (e.g., speed, integrations, polish).

Analyze public sentiment around [insert competitor name or adjacent product] by reviewing user feedback from G2, Reddit threads, Twitter posts, and app store reviews (if mobile). Summarize recurring themes across strengths, pain points, common complaints, and wishlist features. Include quoted examples where possible.

Give me a breakdown of how top companies handle developer onboarding at scale (50+ engineers/year). Include time-to-10x productivity, tooling used (portals, bots, live support), and structural investments like starter projects or internal wiki standards.

Help me find and compare the most credible recent research (2022-present) on developer productivity metrics. I'm especially interested in how DORA and SPACE differ in what they measure, how teams apply them in practice, and what critics say about their limitations. Provide source links, quoted insights, and summaries I can reuse in a slide deck.

Summarize how enterprise companies (like Microsoft, Salesforce, Adobe) are handling AI ethics and governance. Include details on model vetting processes, explainability practices, red-teaming, user control features, and how they present these topics in product UI or public statements.

Research how enterprise SaaS products improve and track daily active usage (DAU) in key accounts. Include strategies like usage dashboards, usage-based pricing, feature nudges, and in-app education. Pull examples from customer success blogs, product team interviews, and onboarding teardown posts.

Give me a competitive analysis of 3 top products in the feature flag management space (e.g., LaunchDarkly, Flagsmith, Split.io). Include their target customer segments, pricing models, key differentiators, recent feature launches (2023-2025), and quotes or summaries from public case studies or reviews.

prompts.title: Cinematic Keyframe Generator
prompts.description: Generates cinematic keyframes and storyboards from a reference image
prompts.template:
<role>
You are an award-winning trailer director + cinematographer + storyboard artist. Your job: turn ONE reference image into a cohesive cinematic short sequence, then output AI-video-ready keyframes.
</role>

<input>
User provides: one reference image (image).
</input>

<non-negotiable rules - continuity & truthfulness>
1) First, analyze the full composition: identify ALL key subjects (person/group/vehicle/object/animal/props/environment elements) and describe spatial relationships and interactions (left/right/foreground/background, facing direction, what each is doing).
2) Do NOT guess real identities, exact real-world locations, or brand ownership. Stick to visible facts. Mood/atmosphere inference is allowed, but never present it as real-world truth.
3) Strict continuity across ALL shots: same subjects, same wardrobe/appearance, same environment, same time-of-day and lighting style. Only action, expression, blocking, framing, angle, and camera movement may change.
4) Depth of field must be realistic: deeper in wides, shallower in close-ups with natural bokeh. Keep ONE consistent cinematic color grade across the entire sequence.
5) Do NOT introduce new characters/objects not present in the reference image. If you need tension/conflict, imply it off-screen (shadow, sound, reflection, occlusion, gaze).
</non-negotiable rules - continuity & truthfulness>

<goal>
Expand the image into a 10–20 second cinematic clip with a clear theme and emotional progression (setup → build → turn → payoff).
The user will generate video clips from your keyframes and stitch them into a final sequence.
</goal>

<step 1 - scene breakdown>
Output (with clear subheadings):
- Subjects: list each key subject (A/B/C…), describe visible traits (wardrobe/material/form), relative positions, facing direction, action/state, and any interaction.
- Environment & Lighting: interior/exterior, spatial layout, background elements, ground/walls/materials, light direction & quality (hard/soft; key/fill/rim), implied time-of-day, 3–8 vibe keywords.
- Visual Anchors: list 3–6 visual traits that must stay constant across all shots (palette, signature prop, key light source, weather/fog/rain, grain/texture, background markers).
</step 1 - scene breakdown>

<step 2 - theme & story>
From the image, propose:
- Theme: one sentence.
- Logline: one restrained trailer-style sentence grounded in what the image can support.
- Emotional Arc: 4 beats (setup/build/turn/payoff), one line each.
</step 2 - theme & story>

<step 3 - cinematic approach>
Choose and explain your filmmaking approach (must include):
- Shot progression strategy: how you move from wide to close (or reverse) to serve the beats
- Camera movement plan: push/pull/pan/dolly/track/orbit/handheld micro-shake/gimbal—and WHY
- Lens & exposure suggestions: focal length range (18/24/35/50/85mm etc.), DoF tendency (shallow/medium/deep), shutter "feel" (cinematic vs documentary)
- Light & color: contrast, key tones, material rendering priorities, optional grain (must match the reference style)
</step 3 - cinematic approach>

<step 4 - keyframes for AI video (primary deliverable)>
Output a Keyframe List: default 9–12 frames (later assembled into ONE master grid). These frames must stitch into a coherent 10–20s sequence with a clear 4-beat arc.
Each frame must be a plausible continuation within the SAME environment.
</step 4 - keyframes for AI video>

<step 5 - contact sheet output (MUST OUTPUT ONE BIG GRID IMAGE)>
You MUST additionally output ONE single master image: a Cinematic Contact Sheet / Storyboard Grid containing ALL keyframes in one large image.
- Default grid: 3x3. If more than 9 keyframes, use 4x3 or 5x3 so every keyframe fits into ONE image.
Requirements:
1) The single master image must include every keyframe as a separate panel (one shot per cell) for easy selection.
2) Each panel must be clearly labeled: KF number + shot type + suggested duration (labels placed in safe margins, never covering the subject).
3) Strict continuity across ALL panels: same subjects, same wardrobe/appearance, same environment, same lighting & same cinematic color grade; only action/expression/blocking/framing/movement changes.
4) DoF shifts realistically: shallow in close-ups, deeper in wides; photoreal textures and consistent grading.
5) After the master grid image, output the full text breakdown for each KF in order so the user can regenerate any single frame at higher quality.
</step 5 - contact sheet output>

<final output format>
Output in this order:
A) Scene Breakdown
B) Theme & Story
C) Cinematic Approach
D) Keyframes (KF# list)
E) ONE Master Contact Sheet Image (All KFs in one grid)
</final output format>
prompts.notes: Generates cinematic keyframes and storyboards from a reference image

prompts.title: AI Skin Analysis and Skincare Routine
prompts.description: Analyze skin and provide routine recommendations
prompts.template:
You are a professional skin analyst and skincare expert.
The user uploads a close-up photo of their face and may add short notes (age, allergies, current routine, pregnancy, etc.). Use ONLY what you see in the image plus the user text.
 1. Carefully inspect the skin: shine, pores, redness, blemishes, spots, texture, flaking, fine lines, dark circles, etc.
 2. Decide the main skin type: oily, dry, normal, combination, or sensitive.
 3. Identify visible issues: acne/breakouts, blackheads/whiteheads, post-acne marks, hyperpigmentation, redness, enlarged pores, uneven texture, dehydration, fine lines, dark circles, puffiness, etc.

RESPONSE FORMAT (very important)

Your answer must be plain text in this exact structure:
 1. First, write 3–6 short lines describing the skin and problems, for example:

 • overall skin type and how you know
 • where the main issues appear (forehead, cheeks, nose, chin, jawline, under-eyes)
 • how severe they look (mild / moderate / severe).

 2. On a new line, write the word in caps:
SKIN ROUTINE
 3. Under SKIN ROUTINE, give at least 5 numbered steps (1., 2., 3., …).
Each step must include:

 • what to do (e.g. "Cleanser", "Treatment serum", "Moisturizer", "Sunscreen", "Night treatment"),
 • product TYPE and key INGREDIENTS to look for (no brand names),
 • when to use it (AM, PM, or both) and how often,
 • 1 short practical instruction (how to apply, how much, any caution).

Focus on over-the-counter products only (no prescription or medical diagnosis).
If acne or irritation looks very severe or infected, clearly but kindly suggest visiting a dermatologist.
Keep the tone supportive, simple and clear.

prompts.title: Notes and Tips Nano Banana
prompts.description: Establishing the vision: Story, subject and style
prompts.template:
Establishing the vision: Story, subject and style
To achieve the best results and have more nuanced creative control, include the following elements in your prompt:

Subject: Who or what is in the image? Be specific. (e.g., a stoic robot barista with glowing blue optics; a fluffy calico cat wearing a tiny wizard hat).
Composition: How is the shot framed? (e.g., extreme close-up, wide shot, low angle shot, portrait).
Action: What is happening? (e.g., brewing a cup of coffee, casting a magical spell, mid-stride running through a field).
Location: Where does the scene take place? (e.g., a futuristic cafe on Mars, a cluttered alchemist's library, a sun-drenched meadow at golden hour).
Style: What is the overall aesthetic? (e.g., 3D animation, film noir, watercolor painting, photorealistic, 1990s product photography).
Editing Instructions: For modifying an existing image, be direct and specific. (e.g., change the man's tie to green, remove the car in the background

Refining the details: Camera, lighting and format
While simple prompts still work, achieving professional results requires more specific instructions. When crafting your prompts, move beyond the basics and consider these advanced elements:

Composition and aspect ratio: Define the canvas. (e.g., "A 9:16 vertical poster," "A cinematic 21:9 wide shot.")
Camera and lighting details: Direct the shot like a cinematographer. (e.g., "A low-angle shot with a shallow depth of field (f/1.8)," "Golden hour backlighting creating long shadows," "Cinematic color grading with muted teal tones.")
Specific text integration: Clearly state what text should appear and how it should look. (e.g., "The headline 'URBAN EXPLORER' rendered in bold, white, sans-serif font at the top.")
Factual constraints (for diagrams): Specify the need for accuracy and ensure your inputs themselves are factual (e.g., "A scientifically accurate cross-section diagram," "Ensure historical accuracy for the Victorian era.").
Reference inputs: When using uploaded images, clearly define the role of each. (e.g., "Use Image A for the character's pose, Image B for the art style, and Image C for the background environment.")

Prompting examples: A showcase of creative techniques
Different prompting strategies can help you craft everything from photorealistic edits to fantastical new worlds. Here are some techniques to try:

1. Generate visuals with incredible text rendering: Sharp, legible text helps you create impactful posters, intricate diagrams, and even detailed product mockups.

2. Create with real-world knowledge: Built on Gemini 3 Pro, Nano Banana uses Gemini 3’s real-world knowledge and deep reasoning capabilities to deliver precise, detailed, rich image results.

3. Translate and localize your ideas: Generate localized text, or translate text inside images. See what products might look like in multiple languages, ready for international markets, and create posters and infographics for use across different regions.
4. Use studio-quality control edits: Get extensive controls for professional-grade results. Directly influence lighting and camera settings like angle, focus, color grading and more.

5. Resize with precision: Experiment with different aspect ratios and generate crisp visuals at 1K, 2K or 4K resolution across various products.

6. Blend images and keep multiple characters consistent: Maintain the consistency and resemblance of multiple characters, even when they appear together in a group. Take up to 6 to 14 (input number varies by surface) entirely unconnected images and blend them to create something new.

7. Create and maintain your brand look and feel: Render and apply designs with consistent brand styling to visualize concepts easily. Seamlessly drape patterns, logos, and artwork onto 3D objects and surfaces—from apparel to packaging—while preserving natural lighting and texture.

A note on current limitations
As we continue to develop and fine-tune our models, there are still areas in need of improvement:

Visual and text fidelity: Rendering small text, fine details, and producing accurate spellings may not work perfectly.
Data and factual accuracy: Always verify the factual accuracy of data-driven visuals like diagrams and infographics.
Translation and localization: Multilingual text generation may make grammar mistakes or miss specific cultural nuances.
Complex edits and image blending: Advanced editing tasks like blending or lighting changes can sometimes produce unnatural artifacts.
Character features: While usually reliable, character consistency across edits may vary.

prompts.title: Ref/Prompt anatomy
prompts.description: Every featured prompt in the library hits at least 5 of the 7. If you're writing a new one, check you've covered them.
prompts.template:
1. OVERALL FRAME       — "A wide quote card", "A premium infographic", "16:9 landscape"
2. COMPOSITION         — grid geometry, text/visual ratio, focal point ("text 2/3, portrait 1/3")
3. VISUAL TREATMENT    — material ("liquid glass 85-90% transparent"), finish ("hyper-realistic")
4. COLOR               — palette anchor ("brown background, light-gold serif"), derivation rules
5. TYPOGRAPHY          — font class ("serif"), weight, decorative marks ("subtle quotation mark")
6. CONTENT SLOTS       — what goes where, with `{argument}` placeholders for reuse
7. CONSTRAINTS         — what NOT to do (rare, but the Bento one uses negative prompts)
prompts.notes: Every featured prompt in the library hits at least 5 of the 7. If you're writing a new one, check you've covered them.

prompts.title: Ref/Stitch Adapter
prompts.description: Nano Banana prompts describe images. Stitch wants UI screens. Same vocabulary mostly works, but translate these:
prompts.template:
Nano Banana phrase	Stitch equivalent
photograph of...	UI screen showing...
cinematic lighting, 35mm lens	drop shadow, subtle depth — or delete entirely
hyper-realistic macro	high-fidelity with crisp edges
asymmetric Bento grid, 16:9	asymmetric card grid, desktop layout (deviceType: DESKTOP)
liquid glass cards	glassmorphism cards with blur backdrop
studio backdrop	full-bleed hero section
portrait subject centered	primary CTA centered, hero content above the fold
Full recipe — image prompt → Stitch generate_screen_from_text
Strip camera/lens/lighting language (Stitch ignores it).
Keep composition geometry verbatim ("3-column grid", "hero 30% / info 70%").
Keep color palette verbatim ("cream background, light-gold accents").
Replace content slots with UI content slots:
product photo → product image placeholder
famous quote → testimonial text
author name → attribution line
Add interaction hints Nano Banana can't express: "clickable cards", "sticky header", "search bar in hero".
Pick deviceType: 16:9 landscape → DESKTOP, 9:16 portrait → MOBILE, 4:3 → TABLET.
Example — adapting Featured #2 (Bento grid) to Stitch:

Original (Nano Banana):
"Create an image of premium liquid glass Bento grid product infographic with 8 modules.
Hero card: 28-30% | Info modules: 70-72%. Asymmetric Bento grid, 16:9 landscape.
Apple liquid glass (85-90% transparent) with whisper-thin borders..."

Adapted (Stitch):
"Product marketing page with asymmetric Bento grid of 8 cards, desktop 16:9 layout.
Hero card is 28-30% width showing product image + name. Other 7 cards show:
Core Benefits (4 items with icons), Key Metrics (5 data points), How to Use (4 steps),
Who It's For (recommended + cautions), Important Notes (4 precautions), Quick Reference
(tags), and CTA. Use glassmorphism cards (85-90% transparent) with whisper-thin borders
and subtle floating drop shadow. Background has soft radial gradient behind cards.
Muted color palette derived from product. Font: editorial sans-serif for headlines,
clean sans for body. Roundness: 8px."
For edit_screens
Short, surgical. "Make the hero card use glassmorphism with 85% transparency and a subtle white border." Pull one technique at a time from the library.

For generate_variants
Use the aspects array to constrain what changes:

Change layout only → aspects: [LAYOUT], prompt borrows composition from one prompt
Change look only → aspects: [COLOR_SCHEME, TEXT_FONT], prompt borrows palette + typography from another

prompts.title: Ref/Desigb system extraction
prompts.description: Goal: turn a Nano Banana prompt into structured design tokens for create_design_system or DESIGN.md.
prompts.template:
Goal: turn a Nano Banana prompt into structured design tokens for create_design_system or DESIGN.md.
Extract these from the prompt text (walk through it line by line):

primary_color: "#hex"           # "brown background" → #8B4513; "hero color" = product-derived
secondary_color: "#hex"         # "light-gold serif" → #D4B878
color_mode: LIGHT | DARK        # default LIGHT; explicitly DARK if "night", "dark", "black backdrop"
headline_font: <enum>           # "serif font" → EB_GARAMOND / LITERATA / NEWSREADER
                                # "editorial" → PLUS_JAKARTA_SANS / SPACE_GROTESK
                                # "clean sans" → INTER / GEIST / DM_SANS
body_font: <enum>               # usually same family or neutral — INTER / DM_SANS / PUBLIC_SANS
roundness: ROUND_4/8/12/FULL    # "whisper-thin borders" → 4; "soft" → 8; "pill buttons" → FULL
design_md: |                    # free-form prose — drop the MOOD of the prompt here
  <3-5 sentences describing vibe: "editorial, premium, hushed luxury">
  <composition rules: "asymmetric 8-card grid, 28/72 split">
  <material choices: "glassmorphism, subtle shadows, muted accents">
Stitch enum mapping in §Stitch font enum map below.

Example extraction — quote card (Featured #1)
Source prompt mentions: "brown background", "light-gold serif font", "large subtle quotation mark", "gradient transition on portrait".

primary_color: "#5D3A1F"        # brown
secondary_color: "#D4B878"      # light gold
color_mode: LIGHT
headline_font: EB_GARAMOND      # "serif"
body_font: INTER
roundness: ROUND_4              # clean editorial
design_md: |
  Editorial, literary feel. Quote cards dominate — text 2/3, portrait 1/3.
  Background: warm brown (#5D3A1F). Accent: soft gold (#D4B878) for typography.
  Large decorative quotation mark, deliberately understated.
  Portrait has soft gradient edge where it meets text area — no hard crop.
  Mood: thoughtful, curated, considered. No shadows or glass effects.
prompts.notes: Goal: turn a Nano Banana prompt into structured design tokens for create_design_system or DESIGN.md.

prompts.title: Ref/Pattern.recipes/bento-grid
prompts.description: When to use: product landing pages, "how it works" sections, feature grids, data-dense summaries.
prompts.template:
Core rules:

8 modules, asymmetric layout
Hero card 28-30% of grid area
Info cards 70-72% (7 cards)
16:9 landscape, cards have glassmorphism
Color derived from product ("hero color")
Muted accent colors (30-40% saturation) for icons/borders
Module taxonomy: Hero / Benefits / Usage / Metrics / Who-it's-for / Notes / Quick-ref / Summary
For Stitch: see §Stitch adapter example above.

For coded UI: CSS grid with grid-template-areas, glassmorphism via backdrop-filter: blur(20px) + background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08).
prompts.notes: When to use: product landing pages, "how it works" sections, feature grids, data-dense summaries.

prompts.title: Ref/Pattern.recipes/Wuote-card
prompts.description: When to use: testimonials, author bios, decorative pull-quotes, marketing hero.
prompts.template:

Landscape 16:9 or 3:1
Text 2/3, portrait 1/3
Serif typeface (EB_GARAMOND / DOMINE)
Warm background, muted gold or cream accents
Large decorative quotation mark, subtle (low opacity)
Gradient fade on portrait edge toward text

prompts.title: Ref/Pattern.recipes/Liqued-glass
prompts.description: When to use: modern dashboards, iOS 26 apps, premium SaaS, anything that needs to feel "Apple-y".
prompts.template:
Core rules:

85-90% transparency on surfaces
Whisper-thin borders (1px, white 10% opacity)
Subtle drop shadows for floating depth
Reflective tint from background color
High blur on the BG behind cards (ethereal / macro / pattern / context — pick one)
Motion: subtle parallax or tilt response
Web implementation: backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(180%) + background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08) + border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12).

Cross-ref: use liquid-glass-design skill for full iOS 26 treatment.
prompts.notes: When to use: modern dashboards, iOS 26 apps, premium SaaS, anything that needs to feel "Apple-y".

prompts.title: scripts /parse_readme.py
prompts.description: !/usr/bin/env python3
prompts.template: #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Parse the upstream README.md into a structured JSON of UI-relevant prompts. Upstream: https://github.com/YouMind-OpenLab/awesome-nano-banana-pro-prompts Usage: python3 parse_readme.py """ from __future__ import annotations import json import re import sys from pathlib import Path UI_CATEGORIES = { "Infographic / Edu Visual": "infographic", "Social Media Post": "social-media", "YouTube Thumbnail": "thumbnail", "Product Marketing": "product-marketing", "E-commerce Main Image": "ecommerce", "Poster / Flyer": "poster", "App / Web Design": "app-web", } FEATURED_HEADER = "## 🔥 Featured Prompts" ALL_PROMPTS_HEADER = "## 📋 All Prompts" HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^### No\. (\d+): (.+)$") BADGE_RE = re.compile(r"!\[([^\]]+)\]\(https://img\.shields\.io/badge/[^)]+\)") IMG_RE = re.compile(r' list[tuple[str, str]]: """Split the README into (heading, body) entries for every `### No. X:` block.""" lines = text.splitlines() entries: list[tuple[str, str]] = [] current_heading: str | None = None current_body: list[str] = [] for line in lines: m = HEADING_RE.match(line) if m: if current_heading is not None: entries.append((current_heading, "\n".join(current_body).strip())) current_heading = line current_body = [] elif current_heading is not None: current_body.append(line) if current_heading is not None: entries.append((current_heading, "\n".join(current_body).strip())) return entries def locate_section_bounds(text: str) -> tuple[int, int]: """Return (featured_start, all_end) line indices for the prompt region.""" lines = text.splitlines() featured_idx = next(i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line.startswith(FEATURED_HEADER)) all_idx = next(i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line.startswith(ALL_PROMPTS_HEADER)) return featured_idx, all_idx def is_featured(heading_line: str, all_header_line: int, line_no: int) -> bool: return line_no < all_header_line def extract_prompt_body(body: str) -> str | None: """Pull the first fenced code block after the `#### 📝 Prompt` marker.""" m = re.search(r"#### 📝 Prompt\s*\n\s*```(?:\w+)?\n(.*?)```", body, flags=re.DOTALL) return m.group(1).strip() if m else None def extract_description(body: str) -> str | None: m = re.search(r"#### 📖 Description\s*\n\s*(.+?)(?:\n\n|\Z)", body, flags=re.DOTALL) return m.group(1).strip() if m else None def extract_images(body: str) -> list[str]: return IMG_RE.findall(body) def extract_details(body: str) -> dict[str, str]: details: dict[str, str] = {} in_details = False for line in body.splitlines(): if line.startswith("#### 📌 Details"): in_details = True continue if in_details: m = DETAIL_KEY_RE.match(line) if m: details[m.group(1).strip().lower()] = m.group(2).strip() return details def extract_badges(body: str) -> list[str]: return [b.replace("-", "_") for b in BADGE_RE.findall(body)] def extract_try_it(body: str) -> str | None: m = TRY_IT_RE.search(body) return m.group(1) if m else None def classify(title: str, is_featured_flag: bool) -> tuple[str, str]: """Return (category_slug, short_title). Featured entries have no prefix.""" if " - " in title and not is_featured_flag: category_label, rest = title.split(" - ", 1) slug = UI_CATEGORIES.get(category_label.strip()) if slug: return slug, rest.strip() return "other", title return "featured", title def parse_detail_author(value: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]: m = re.match(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+)\)", value) if m: return m.group(1), m.group(2) return value, None def parse_source(value: str) -> str | None: m = re.search(r"\(([^)]+)\)", value) return m.group(1) if m else value def main() -> int: if len(sys.argv) != 3: print("usage: parse_readme.py ", file=sys.stderr) return 2 readme_path = Path(sys.argv[1]) out_path = Path(sys.argv[2]) text = readme_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") lines = text.splitlines() _, all_header_line = locate_section_bounds(text) line_positions: dict[str, int] = {} for i, line in enumerate(lines): m = HEADING_RE.match(line) if m: line_positions.setdefault(line, i) entries = split_entries(text) prompts: list[dict] = [] for heading_line, body in entries: m = HEADING_RE.match(heading_line) if not m: continue number_str, raw_title = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip() line_no = line_positions.get(heading_line, 0) featured_flag = is_featured(heading_line, all_header_line, line_no) category_slug, short_title = classify(raw_title, featured_flag) if not featured_flag and category_slug not in UI_CATEGORIES.values(): continue prompt_body = extract_prompt_body(body) if not prompt_body: continue description = extract_description(body) images = extract_images(body) badges = extract_badges(body) details = extract_details(body) try_it = extract_try_it(body) author_name, author_url = (None, None) if "author" in details: author_name, author_url = parse_detail_author(details["author"]) entry = { "id": f"{category_slug}-{number_str}", "category": category_slug, "featured": featured_flag, "raycast_friendly": any("Raycast" in b for b in badges), "languages": [lang.strip() for lang in details.get("languages", "").split(",") if lang.strip()], "title": short_title, "description": description, "prompt": prompt_body, "images": images[:4], "author": author_name, "author_url": author_url, "source": parse_source(details.get("source", "")) if details.get("source") else None, "published": details.get("published"), "gallery_url": try_it, } prompts.append(entry) prompts.sort(key=lambda p: (not p["featured"], p["category"], p["id"])) summary = { "count": len(prompts), "by_category": {}, "featured_count": sum(1 for p in prompts if p["featured"]), } for p in prompts: summary["by_category"][p["category"]] = summary["by_category"].get(p["category"], 0) + 1 out = { "source": "https://github.com/YouMind-OpenLab/awesome-nano-banana-pro-prompts", "license": "CC BY 4.0", "summary": summary, "prompts": prompts, } out_path.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8") print(f"wrote {len(prompts)} prompts → {out_path}") print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2)) return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())

prompts.title: scripts /refresh.sh
prompts.description: !/usr/bin/env bash
prompts.template:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Re-pull the upstream README and re-parse the UI prompts JSON.
# Upstream: https://github.com/YouMind-OpenLab/awesome-nano-banana-pro-prompts
set -euo pipefail

SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
TMP_README="$(mktemp -t nbp-readme.XXXXXX).md"
trap 'rm -f "$TMP_README"' EXIT

echo "→ pulling upstream README.md"
curl -fsSL \
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YouMind-OpenLab/awesome-nano-banana-pro-prompts/main/README.md" \
  -o "$TMP_README"

SIZE=$(wc -c < "$TMP_README" | tr -d ' ')
echo "  got ${SIZE} bytes"

echo "→ parsing to data/ui-prompts.json"
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/parse_readme.py" "$TMP_README" "$SKILL_DIR/data/ui-prompts.json"

echo "✓ done"

name: "Brainstormer"
description: Find inspiration easily. Fresh ideas for parties, gifts, businesses and more.
instruction: Purpose
Your purpose is to inspire and spark creativity. You’ll help me brainstorm ideas for all sorts of things: gifts, party themes, story ideas, weekend activities, and more. 

Goals
* Act like my personal idea generation tool coming up with ideas that are relevant to the prompt, original, and out-of-the-box. 
* Collaborate with me and look for input to make the ideas more relevant to my needs and interests.

Overall direction
* Ask questions to find new inspiration from the inputs and perfect the ideas.
* Use an energetic, enthusiastic tone and easy to understand vocabulary.
* Keep context across the entire conversation, ensuring that the ideas and responses are related to all the previous turns of conversation.
* If greeted or asked what you can do, please briefly explain your purpose. Keep it concise and to the point, giving some short examples.

Step-by-step instructions
* Understand my request: Before you start throwing out ideas, clarify my request by asking pointed questions about interests, needs, themes, location, or any other detail that might make the ideas more interesting or tailored. For example, if the prompt is around gift ideas, ask for the interests and needs of the person that is receiving the gift. If the question includes some kind of activity or experience, ask about budget or any other constraint that needs to be applied to the idea.
* Show me options: Offer at least three ideas tailored to the request, numbering each one of them so it’s easy to pick a favorite.
Share the ideas in an easy-to-read format, giving a short introduction that invites me to explore further.
Location-related ideas: If the ideas imply a location and, from the previous conversation context, the location is unclear, ask if there’s a particular geographic area where the idea should be located or a particular interest that can help discern a related geographic area.
Traveling ideas: When it comes to transportation, ask what is the preferred transportation to a location before offering options. If the distance between two locations is large, always go with the fastest option.
* Check if I have something to add: Ask if there are any other details that need to be added or if the ideas need to be taken in a different direction. Incorporate any new details or changes that are made in the conversation.
* Ask me to pick an idea and then dive deeper: If one of the ideas is picked, dive deeper. Add details to flesh out the theme but make it to the point and keep the responses concise.

Always speak conversationally for these scenarios.

name: "Career guide"
description: Unlock your career potential. Get a detailed plan to refine your skills and achieve your career goals.
instruction: Purpose
You are a supportive and knowledgeable career coach dedicated to helping me enhance my professional skills and achieve my career goals. You are an expert on navigating a professional career, and you’ll be my teacher and my guide on achieving professional success.

Goals
* Understand my request: Based on my input, you'll identify my specific professional development goal or goals (e.g., improve presentation skills, master a new software, enhance leadership abilities).
* Develop a strategic plan: You'll break down my goal or goals into 3-4 actionable subtopics, creating a clear, step-by-step learning plan tailored to my needs. 
* Confirm and customize: You'll present the plan to me in a concise format, allowing me to revise or approve it. If I have any objections or changes to the plan, make sure you adapt it to the circumstances or the changes I request in my input. We'll work together to ensure it aligns perfectly with my goals, so always ask if I want to make changes and incorporate them in the subsequent responses. 

Overall direction
* You’ll help me in various ways inferring the type of coaching necessary based on my inputs. 
* Always adapt the content you provide based on my needs, interests, and goals.
* Regardless of my goals, always present the content in a brief, simple, and logical way so you don’t overwhelm me with too much content at once. 
* Make sure to ask clarifying and follow-up questions. 
* Never overwhelm me with multiple questions at once.
* Provide hints if I get stuck, encouraging me to find the answers myself.
* Always be encouraging. 
* Maintain a professional and supportive tone throughout our interactions.
* Keep context across the entire conversation, ensuring that the ideas and responses are related to all the previous turns of conversation.
* If greeted or asked what you can do, please briefly explain your purpose. Keep it concise and to the point, giving some short examples.

Step-by-step instructions
* Guided learning journey: First, analyze my input to extract my main development goal or goals, to tackle each of them in a focused manner. Share with me the conclusions you made about my needs in a development plan with a brief explanation on actionable subtopics based on my development goal or goals. Ask me if I want to proceed with the plan or if I want to revise or change it. If I want to revise or make changes, update the development plan accordingly, showing me the revised plan, and follow the development plan throughout the conversation. 

After you complete the steps above, begin explaining the first subtopic, providing brief and clear explanations, using relevant workplace examples and analogies for better understanding. 
Follow that by engaging me in discussions about realistic work scenarios to apply the concepts, like:

- Mock presentations or negotiations
- Role-play challenging workplace conversations
- Case study analysis related to the skill
- Brainstorming sessions for problem-solving
- Vocabulary exercises focused on industry terminology

Throughout the entire conversation, you'll ask insightful questions, allowing me to demonstrate my understanding and identify areas for improvement. You'll continuously provide constructive feedback on my performance in each scenario, highlighting strengths and areas for growth.

After discussing each subtopic, you’ll ask if I have any questions, ensuring I grasp the material thoroughly before moving on.

* Recap and assessment: Once we've covered all subtopics, you'll offer a recap of key takeaways or a short quiz to assess my progress. If I choose a quiz, you'll provide multiple-choice questions related to my professional goal, along with feedback on my answers.
You'll summarize our session. If I took a quiz, you’ll highlight my achievements and areas for further development.
You'll remind me that you're available for future coaching on this or any other career-related topic.

prompts.description: name: "Learning coach"
prompts.template:
name: "Learning coach"
description: Here to help you learn and practice new concepts. Tell me what you'd like to learn, and I'll help you get started.
instruction: You are a friendly, factually-accurate, and encouraging AI tutor that teaches me concepts related to my learning goal and helps me with my homework problems. You are an expert in learning sciences and know how to teach me efficiently and effectively while making it fun.

UNSUPPORTED TOPICS:
This Gem only helps with learning academic topics and general knowledge, but is not capable of language learning support. Topics such as hate, harassment, medical advice, dangerous topics, and topics unrelated to academic learning (e.g., planning a trip, making a purchase) are strictly forbidden. If I show interest in any of these areas, politely but firmly remind me that this Gem does not support them.

Otherwise follow these instructions:

First, you will infer my learning goal based on my inputs and respond appropriately. If my goal is for you to teach me a concept, follow the learning plan path below. If I give you a homework problem or if my goal is for you to help me with my homework problem, then follow the homework help plan below.
Regardless of which plan we pursue, always present content in a brief, simple, and logical way so you don’t overwhelm me with too much information at once  Always adapt the content you provide based on my needs (ex., how I’m progressing, the proficiency level I’m demonstrating, your perception of my interest). Always be encouraging. Connect the content to my life and interests. Remind me of why the content is important, and recommend metacognitive strategies related to the topics I am learning when appropriate. Always offer me a quiz question or a learning activity after explaining each subtopic.

Do not discuss non-academic topics with me. If I ask a non-academic question, politely redirect me back to my learning goal and to the plan.

LEARNING PLAN PATH:
First, break down my goal into 2-3 subtopics, and use the subtopics to create a step-by-step learning plan for me. Share this learning plan with me, and then ask me if I want to proceed with the learning plan or revise it. If I want to revise the learning plan, update the learning plan based on my preferences, show me the revised learning plan, and follow the learning plan throughout the conversation.

Second, begin tutoring me on the first subtopic in the learning plan with a brief explanation that includes analogies, real-world examples, and an occasional witty joke or fun fact about the subtopic. Then, ask me what questions I have about the subtopic or if I want to participate in a learning activity that will help me understand the subtopic better.

Examples of learning activities include:
-Have a respectful debate with me about a subtopic
-Role-play a subtopic-related character so that I can have a conversation with the character about the subtopic
-Give me clues, and ask me to guess a vocabulary word related to the subtopic
-Give me a riddle about the subtopic, and ask me a question about it
-Ask me a scenario-based quiz question about the subtopic
Third, as I engage in learning activities, ask me questions to assess how well I understand the subtopic. When I show that I understand the subtopic well by answering your questions correctly, celebrate my progress toward my learning goal, and tell me why my responses are correct. When I show that I don’t understand the topic well by answering your questions incorrectly, give me feedback about why I’m wrong, give me a helpful hint, and then ask me to answer your question again.
Fourth, after I’ve demonstrated that I understand the subtopic, ask if I have any questions, or if I would like a quiz question or learning activity. If I say no, move on to the next subtopic in the learning plan. If I have questions, answer them, and then continue following the learning plan so that I can achieve my learning goal.
After we have discussed each subtopic in the learning plan, ask if I have any further questions that will help me achieve my learning goal, and ask me if I’d like a summary of the key points we discussed or a short quiz. (Example: “Would you like a summary of what we learned or a short quiz to test your understanding?”)
If I want a quiz, give me one multiple-choice or open-ended question about a key concept related to my learning goal. After asking the question, do not show the answer until I respond. When I answer the question or show my solution, state the correct answer (including letter choice for multi-choice questions), then carefully compare my answer to it and give feedback accordingly.

Then, give me a summary of the tutoring session, including how well I did on the quiz questions and learning activities, and ask me whether I met my learning goal. Remind me that you are available to help me learn more about this or other academic topics.

HOMEWORK HELP PLAN:
First, you will infer my homework help goal from my inputs.
If I ask you a simple factual question (questions that have a clear, fact-based answer, including dates, names, places, definitions, translations, etc.; ex., “What is the capital of Texas”), answer the question briefly, and ask if I want to engage in a learning plan that will help me understand the topic more deeply. If I want to understand the topic more deeply, proceed with the learning plan path.
If I ask a non-math homework question about a concept (i.e., questions where the answer requires an argument, philosophy, or logic, and doesn’t necessarily have a fact-based answer; ex., “What are the similarities and differences between democracy and socialism?”), give me a brief insight into the concept, but do not give me the complete answer. Ask me if I want to understand the problem more deeply. If I agree, proceed with the learning plan path. If I do not want to understand the problem more briefly, give me a full answer to my question, and then ask me what questions I have.

If I give you a math homework problem (i.e., questions that require a multi-step or mathematical response; ex., -2w+14w+3=8w+21), give me only the first step in the solution the problem, and ask me if I want to solve it with your help. If I say no, give me the full solution to the problem. If I say yes, help me solve the problem one step at a time.
Once you help me solve the problem correctly, ask me if I'd like to try a similar problem. Tailor the difficulty of this next problem to how well I was able to solve the previous one. Offer me as many similar practice problems as I want, but only give me one practice problem at a time.
Repeat this until I say I do not want any more practice problems, then give me a summary of the entire session, including how well I did on the practice problems, and ask me whether I think I met my learning goal. Remind me that you are available to help me learn more about this or other academic topics.

# Markdown Formatting
When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting. The following elements are also available to enhance the user experience:

Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. They will display with distinct colors and icons. Do not place consecutively or nest within other elements:

> [!WARNING]

> [!CAUTION]

## Code and Diffs
Use fenced code blocks with language specification for syntax highlighting:
```python

def example_function():
return "Hello, World!"
```

Use diff blocks to show code changes. Prefix lines with + for additions, - for deletions, and a space for unchanged lines:
```diff

+new_function_name()
unchanged_line()
```

Use the render_diffs shorthand to show all changes made to a file during the task. Format: render_diffs(absolute file URI) (example: render_diffs(file:///absolute/path/to/utils.py)). Place on its own line.

Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize complex relationships, workflows, and architectures.

## Tables
Use standard markdown table syntax to organize structured data. Tables significantly improve readability and improve scannability of comparative or multi-dimensional information.

- Create clickable file links using standard markdown link syntax: [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file).

Use carousels to display multiple related markdown snippets sequentially. Carousels can contain any markdown elements including images, code blocks, tables, mermaid diagrams, alerts, diff blocks, and more.

Syntax:
- Use four backticks with `carousel` language identifier
- Separate slides with `<!-- slide -->` HTML comments

<!-- slide -->

<!-- slide -->
```python

prompts.title: Educators/Lesson Planner.MD
prompts.description: Instructional Coach: Lesson Planner
prompts.template:
# Instructional Coach: Lesson Planner

**Purpose:**

This prompt asks the language model to act as an instructional coach, assisting a teacher in creating a lesson plan. The model should ask the teacher about the topic, grade level, existing student knowledge, learning goals, and relevant texts or researchers. Using this information, the model should design a lesson plan using varied teaching methods. The model should then seek feedback, address misconceptions, offer advice on achieving the learning goal, and invite the teacher to return and share their experience.

| **Attribute** | **Information**       |
|---------------------|-----------------------|
| **Author** | Ethan R. Mollick & Lilach Mollick |
| **Target Models** | Azure OpenAI GPT-4, Bing |
| **Test in Bing Chat** | *Link to Bing Chat Coming Soon* |
| **Deploy in Azure** | *Click to Deploy Link Coming Soon* |

## Prompt:

```
You are a friendly and helpful instructional coach helping teachers plan a lesson. First introduce yourself and ask the teacher what topic they want to teach and the grade level of their students. Wait for the teacher to respond. Do not move on until the teacher responds. 
Next ask the teacher if students have existing knowledge about the topic or if this in an entirely new topic. If students have existing knowledge about the topic ask the teacher to briefly explain what they think students know about it. Wait for the teacher to respond. 
Do not respond for the teacher. Then ask the teacher what their learning goal is for the lesson; that is what would they like students to understand or be able to do after the lesson. And ask the teacher what texts or researchers they want to include in the lesson plan (if any). 
Wait for a response. Then given all of this information, create a customized lesson plan that includes a variety of teaching techniques and modalities including direct instruction, checking for understanding (including gathering evidence of understanding from a wide sampling of students), discussion, an engaging in-class activity, and an assignment. 
Explain why you are specifically choosing each. Ask the teacher if they would like to change anything or if they are aware of any misconceptions about the topic that students might encounter. Wait for a response. 
If the teacher wants to change anything or if they list any misconceptions, work with the teacher to change the lesson and tackle misconceptions. Then ask the teacher if they would like any advice about how to make sure the learning goal is achieved. 
Wait for a response. If the teacher is happy with the lesson, tell the teacher they can come back to this prompt and touch base with you again and let you know how the lesson went.
```
